payload.retro_drained:
KILLER. Inbox 6 at retro start, one more captured during it, 7 dispositioned, inbox 0. Five pulled into this iteration (read/search surface; se_run's fence hole; required-arg enforcement; the model-quality question, now partly answered by v1's guidance; the every-folder ruling). Two routed rather than pulled: the board's new-tab-per-start to i9-board-rounds, and the one-representation/invalidation design to the next phone iteration, per the owner's own words. None rejected.

The drain created one follow-up and I minted it rather than carrying it: the last note MIXED a design request with a shipped bug, so se.raid-hosted-page-claims-a-bless-it-did-not-land now carries the defect on its own - the hosted page reports 'Blessed' on a relay 200 even when the engine bound nothing.

Field feedback answered FIRST, before any gathering, and it steered the whole retro: 'we are making mistakes v1 didn't make in the end - check v1's guidance and put what you learn into ours.' Acting on it inside the retro produced a correction to my own findings, which is the part worth recording: I reported the state-of-the-art check as MISSING from v2. It is not. se.machine-systematic-write-requirements says verbatim 'Position the concrete set against the standard checklists for this deliverable kind', and meth-state-of-the-art rules it for every gate. What is missing is that NOTHING COLLECTS IT - that state's evidence form has two fields and the scan is not one of them. The check did not fail; it was never asked for.
payload.goal: Make the lane the path of LEAST RESISTANCE - and make the machine judge mechanically what it currently asks the agent to assert about its own work.
payload.pulled_in:
ELEVEN items. The first two are the spine; the rest are the backlog that made this iteration necessary.

1. GUIDANCE REACHES THE PACKET (origin: owner, this kickoff). The machine joins ALL applicable guidance onto every evidence form - applies_to matching plus [[wikilink]] resolution - instead of serving one hand-written paragraph per state with unresolved pointers. Planned in i4 as 'guidance registry / packet method-link resolution'; never shipped. THE ARGUMENT THAT MAKES IT URGENT: four laws were minted today, each with an applies_to, and NONE will ever reach a packet. A fresh session tomorrow cannot learn them except by chance. The ledger is accumulating laws that do not bind.

2. THE LINT SWEEP (origin: owner ruling, this kickoff). Walk every machine-state prompt, sort each check into MECHANICAL or JUDGEMENT, build the lint infrastructure if it does not exist, and lint everything mechanical. Rule: if a lint can judge it, the agent does not. First candidates, all self-asserted today: models_adhered (a set comparison between the M4 allocation and what the build touched), red_observed (the run record already proves it), designs_realized and adrs_traced (coverage queries), verifiable and breaks_if_removed (field presence), the state-of-the-art scan's PRESENCE (its quality cannot be linted; its absence can). THIS IS THE SAME ITEM AS SAFE SELF-BLESSING: per se.law-responsibility-never-delegates, the fix for killers passing that should not have is mechanical judgement, never more human review.

3. RIPGREP AS A FIRST-CLASS DEPENDENCY, AND THE NAIVE SEARCHER RIPPED OUT (origin: owner ruling). No fallback, by explicit ruling: 'I don't want duplicate code which we never test and never run.' What it buys: --json (typed events with byte offsets and submatch spans, so search returns structured records instead of scraped text), -C context, -g globs and --files (which is our missing glob for free), -U multiline, -c counts and --max-filesize caps so a huge file degrades to a count, gitignore awareness, -z compressed and --pre preprocessors, -E encoding transcoding. Delete deliverable.ts's literal/ranked/fuzzy search rather than leaving it beside rg. NOT REPLACED: se_get_search's BM25 over ledger nodes - different job, ranked relevance over prose, and genuinely better than grep for guidance.

4. CHUNKED READS: se_file_read gains offset/limit. se-v2-design.md at 132k chars is unreadable through the lane today, which is the leading suspect for three design-doc-to-build losses in i8d.

5. @NAME DECLARED ROOTS, REACHING ANYWHERE (origin: owner, ruled at this kickoff). Declare-once addressing rather than per-call paths, because the audit trail needs semantics: an owner reviewing a delegated iteration must see WHAT was consulted, not where a file sat. SPLIT RULED HERE: the LEDGER carries the name, reason and mode (portable, reviewable, and retirement becomes one deletion when v1 goes at i10); the MACHINE-LOCAL config carries the path (never committed, correct per machine). Reaching an undeclared root returns a typed rejection whose remedy IS the declare call - one-turn recovery, so declaring never blocks. First roots to declare: v1 and the design-doc folder, which closes the three oldest unserved se_help misses.

6. se_config: A LANE FOR THE MACHINE-LOCAL CONFIG. Nothing on the surface reads, writes or validates ~/.se/<project>/*.json today - not for the agent, and not for the OWNER, who currently hand-writes JSON and finds out it was wrong when a card arrives without a link. Now also the home for root paths (5).

7. BATCH PATCHING: se_file_patch gains ops mirroring se_set_apply. Measured, not preferred: 645 calls makes it the most-used product tool by 3x, and 28 failures makes it the most-failing.

8. REQUIRED ARGS ENFORCED AT DISPATCH. A wrong arg name today coerces undefined and the tool answers confidently on garbage.

9. se_run STOPS BEING A HOLE IN THE FENCE. Whitelist: se_file_* is the one writer to the product; se_run's tree is read+execute. Per the owner's ruling the target is INVISIBILITY, not workarounds - working around a gap is legal, hiding it is not.

10. THE RECORD SURVIVES A DELETED TAG. Annotated tags at close (ours are lightweight, so push.followTags would silently push nothing); evidence_commit recorded beside evidence_tag; push.followTags set idempotently so VS Code users carry tags without a flag; iter/* branches deleted after close, provably safe because the merge's second parent holds the record.

11. THE STATE-OF-THE-ART SCAN BECOMES COLLECTED EVIDENCE - the specific instance of (1) and (2) that this retro found, and the one that would have caught i8d's lost bless controls at the requirements gate.
payload.left_out:
WITHDRAWN AFTER THE OWNER CORRECTED ME, and worth recording because I had them wrong: v1's architecture DIAGRAM as a hard-rule killer, and v1's explicit VIEW SELECTION. I reported both as v2 regressions. They are deliberate improvements - v1's diagrams never really worked, and the matrix review IS v2's replacement for both. I was comparing against v1's checklist instead of against what we decided since.

EXPLICITLY RULED OUT: a hand-rolled search fallback beside ripgrep. Owner: duplicate code that is never tested and never run is worse than depending on rg outright. This makes rg load-bearing, accepted knowingly.

ROUTED ELSEWHERE, each with a home: the board's tab-per-start to i9-board-rounds; the one-representation/mutual-invalidation design AND the hosted page's false 'Blessed' to the next phone iteration; the top-level machine rework to i11, which the owner reserved this morning.

NOT PULLED, named so it is not mistaken for an oversight: the call log's tool-name double-counting (se.run/se_run, se_deliverable_* from before a rename) makes automated retro queries undercount. Real, small, and it belongs with the next log-aggregation work rather than widening this iteration.

AND THE THING THIS ITERATION CANNOT FIX: an iteration still cannot exercise its own build through the live surface (se.raid-an-iteration-cannot-run-its-own-build). Every tool built here reaches the running engine only after this iteration merges. That is accepted, now understood exactly - hot reload watches the trunk checkout, worktrees exist to keep the build out of it - and it is not in scope.
payload.rigor:
SYSTEMATIC, unpruned, no strikes.

The temptation is to run this lean: it is 'just tooling', mostly mechanical, and the owner wants it done. I am declining that for a specific reason rather than out of caution. This iteration changes the machinery that JUDGES every future iteration - the guidance that reaches the agent, and the lints that replace the agent's own assertions. A weak check built here is not one weak check; it is a weak check that every later gate leans on while reporting green. That is the exact failure shape the whole day has been about.

The systematic milestones also earn their place concretely here: M1's state-of-the-art scan on the IDEA is real work, since agent file-tool design is an active field and we should position against it rather than invent; M3's scan on the requirement SET is the very check this retro found missing, so running it properly is also its first test; and M5's spike matters because the ripgrep integration has one genuinely unknown leg - whether --json's event stream maps cleanly onto the tool surface we want, and how it behaves across the platforms we actually ship to.

One rigor note carried from the owner's ruling: killers stay agent-blessable under the standing delegation. The answer to today's quality problems is the lint sweep in this iteration's own scope, not a tighter human loop.
